blocks.content: This closing topic connects everything in this module to a forward-looking need: stateful applications, covered in their own dedicated module, require each replica to have its own individual, persistent storage, not storage shared across all of them.
1. Each Replica Needs Its Own Volume
blocks.text: 1. Each Replica Needs Its Own Volume

blocks.content: Unlike a stateless application where any replica is interchangeable, a stateful application, a database cluster node, for instance, needs its own dedicated storage, replica A's data must stay distinctly A's, not merged or shared with replica B's.

blocks.alt: Distinct, individually owned storage per replica, not one shared pool

blocks.content: A stateless Deployment replica, covered in its own module, generally does not care which storage (if any) it gets, any replica is interchangeable. A stateful replica specifically needs its own dedicated storage, tied to its own identity, a genuinely different requirement.

blocks.alt: Interchangeable storage needs versus a genuine one-to-one, per-replica requirement

blocks.content: This is exactly what volumeClaimTemplates, a StatefulSet-specific feature covered in full in the Stateful Applications module, automates, generating one distinct PVC per replica automatically, rather than requiring a hand-crafted PVC for each one.

blocks.alt: One PVC automatically generated per replica, not created by hand

blocks.content: 4. The Two Pillars StatefulSets Are Built On
blocks.text: 4. The Two Pillars StatefulSets Are Built On

blocks.content: Put together with the headless Service covered in the Services module (giving each replica its own stable, individually addressable identity), per-replica persistent storage is the second foundational piece, both together are exactly what the StatefulSet workload type, covered next in this course, is built entirely around.

blocks.alt: Individual network identity and individual storage, the two pillars of StatefulSets

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Stateful applications need per-replica, individually owned storage, not a shared pool, a fundamentally different requirement from stateless Deployments.
This, combined with the individual network identity a headless Service provides, is exactly what the StatefulSet workload type, covered next, is built around.
